en: twisted doughnut; Korean twisted fried dough

examples.ko: 시장에서 갓 튀긴 꽈배기를 사 먹었어요.
examples.en: I bought and ate a freshly fried twisted doughnut at the market.
Twisted doughnuts taste even better coated with sugar.
I ordered a twisted doughnut and coffee as a snack.
I braided my hair into a twisted shape.

examples.ko: 이 집 꽈배기는 겉이 바삭하고 속이 쫄깃해요.
examples.en: This place's twisted doughnuts are crispy outside and chewy inside.

examples.ko: 꽈배기처럼 꼬인 줄을 푸느라 한참 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took a long time to untangle the rope twisted like a pretzel.

explain: 밀가루 반죽을 길게 꼬아서 튀긴 간식이에요. 무언가가 심하게 꼬인 모양을 말할 때 '꽈배기처럼'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: Glutinous rice twisted doughnuts are chewy and delicious.
phrases.nuance_ko: 찹쌀로 만들어 더 쫄깃한 꽈배기를 부르는 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The name for the chewier twisted doughnut made with glutinous rice.

phrases.en: I fried twisted doughnuts at home on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꽈배기를 만드는 과정을 말할 때 '튀기다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs with '튀기다' when talking about making them.

phrases.en: The earphone cord got twisted like a twisted doughnut.
phrases.nuance_ko: 줄이나 끈이 심하게 꼬인 모양을 비유할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A comparison for cords or strings that are badly twisted.

explain_en: It is a snack made of dough twisted into a long shape and fried. People also say '꽈배기처럼' when describing something badly twisted.

examples.en: In summer, jellyfish naengchae whets the appetite.
They served naengchae first as part of the feast.
You pour mustard sauce on this naengchae.
My mother made shrimp naengchae for us.

examples.ko: 냉채는 차게 먹는 요리라서 더운 날 좋아요.
examples.en: Naengchae is eaten cold, so it's nice on a hot day.
I ordered naengchae at a Chinese restaurant and it was refreshing.

explain: 여러 재료를 차게 해서 소스에 버무려 먹는 요리예요. 겨자나 식초가 들어간 새콤한 소스와 자주 먹고, 코스 요리에서는 처음에 나오는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: I poured mustard sauce on the shrimp cold salad.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재료 이름을 앞에 붙여 요리 종류를 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: You can put an ingredient name in front to say what kind of dish it is.

phrases.en: I ordered naengchae at the Chinese restaurant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식당에서 주문하는 상황에 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when ordering at a restaurant.

phrases.en: The naengchae sauce is tangy and gets my appetite going.
phrases.nuance_ko: 냉채에 뿌리는 새콤한 소스를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the tangy sauce poured over naengchae.

explain_en: It is a dish of several ingredients served cold and tossed in a sauce. It is often eaten with a tangy mustard or vinegar sauce and frequently comes first in a set course.

examples.en: I divide the cake equally into eight pieces.
The teacher divided the paper equally into three.
I will divide the field equally into four parts.
I shape the equally divided dough into rounds.

examples.ko: 수학 시간에 선분을 등분하는 방법을 배웠어요.
examples.en: In math class I learned how to divide a line segment equally.
I split my allowance into two equal parts and saved it.

explain: '몇 개로 등분하다'처럼 같은 크기로 나눌 때만 써요. 크기가 달라도 되는 '나누다'와 달리 조각이 모두 똑같아야 해요. 수학이나 요리 설명에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I divide the pizza into four equal pieces.
phrases.nuance_ko: '등분하다'와 뜻이 같지만 일상 대화에서 더 쉽고 자연스럽게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 등분하다, but easier and more natural in everyday talk.

phrases.example: 긴 끈을 다섯 개로 등분해 주세요.
phrases.en: Please divide the long string into five equal parts.
phrases.nuance_ko: '등분하다'로 부탁할 때 쓰는 말이에요. 수학이나 만들기 설명에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite request form of 등분하다, common in math and craft instructions.

phrases.en: We divided the bread into three equal parts and shared it.
phrases.nuance_ko: '등분하다' 앞에 숫자를 붙여 몇 개로 나누는지 정확히 말하는 방법이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds a number before 등분하다 to say exactly how many equal parts.
phrases.en_equiv: to divide into three equal parts

explain_en: Split exactly equally, like a cake into four. Used only when dividing into equal sizes, as in 몇 개로 등분하다. Unlike 나누다, which allows unequal parts, 등분하다 needs every part to be the same size. It shows up often in math and cooking instructions.

gh: divide or share out; the most common word
mark off an area into zones

p.s: 엄마가 케이크를 똑같이 여덟 개로 등분했어요.
p.o: 엄마가 케이크를 똑같이 여덟 개로 나눴어요.
p.n: 등분하다 says the parts are equal; 나누다 does not say that by itself.

t90.ax: I divide the cake equally into eight pieces.

examples.en: Fried tofu sushi is popular as a lunchbox item.
I ate udon with fried tofu in it.
I bought a bag of fried tofu pouches at the mart.
The fried tofu soaks up the broth, so it is delicious.
The child picks out only the fried tofu to eat.

examples.ko: 내일 점심에는 유부를 넣고 김밥을 말 거예요.
examples.en: For lunch tomorrow, I will roll gimbap with fried tofu in it.

explain: 한국에서는 '유부초밥', '유부우동'처럼 다른 음식 이름 안에 넣어 말하는 일이 많아요. 찌개나 부침에 넣는 '두부'와 쓰임이 달라서 둘을 바꿔 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: I packed fried tofu rice pouches for the picnic lunch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 유부 안에 초밥용 밥을 넣은 음식이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A dish with seasoned rice stuffed inside fried tofu.

phrases.en: On cold days, I crave warm fried tofu udon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 유부를 올린 우동을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Udon noodles topped with fried tofu.

phrases.en: I slice the fried tofu thinly and add it to the soup.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요리할 때 쓰는 가장 기본적인 동작이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic action when cooking with it.

explain_en: In Korea this word mostly shows up inside dish names like '유부초밥' and '유부우동'. It is used differently from plain '두부', which goes into stews and pan-fried dishes, so the two are not interchangeable.

en: single-plate dish; à la carte dish

examples.en: This restaurant is famous for its delicious à la carte dishes.
I'll order just one dish à la carte instead of the course.

examples.ko: 점심에는 일품요리를 싸게 파는 곳이 많아요.
examples.en: Many places sell à la carte dishes cheaply at lunch.

examples.ko: 일품요리 메뉴에서 먹고 싶은 걸 골라 보세요.
examples.en: Pick what you want to eat from the à la carte menu.

examples.ko: 오늘은 갈비찜 같은 일품요리가 먹고 싶어요.
examples.en: Today I want an à la carte dish like braised short ribs.
There are many customers, so à la carte orders are delayed.

explain: 메뉴판에서 '코스'나 '정식'과 나란히 나오는 말이에요. 여러 접시가 차례로 나오는 코스와 달리, 갈비찜이나 비빔밥처럼 한 접시로 식사가 되는 요리를 하나씩 골라 시킬 때 써요. '단품'은 세트가 아닌 메뉴 하나를 가리켜서 쓰임이 가깝지만 똑같지는 않아요.

phrases.en: Shall we order à la carte instead of the course today?
phrases.nuance_ko: 식당에서 메뉴를 하나씩 골라 주문할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when choosing and ordering dishes one by one at a restaurant.

phrases.en: They only sell à la carte items at lunch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 메뉴판에서 코스나 정식과 구별되는 칸을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the section of a menu separate from courses and set meals.

phrases.example: 이 메뉴는 단품으로도 주문할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You can also order this menu item on its own.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세트가 아니라 메뉴 하나만 주문한다는 뜻이라 패스트푸드점에서도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means ordering a single item rather than a set, also used at fast-food places.

explain_en: On a menu it appears alongside '코스' (course) and '정식' (set meal). Unlike a course with several plates in order, it is a dish like 갈비찜 or 비빔밥 that works as a meal on one plate and is ordered individually. '단품' (single item) is close in use, but it means one menu item that is not part of a set, so the two are not identical.

examples.en: I get starch from potatoes and use it in cooking.

examples.ko: 탕수육 소스는 전분 물을 넣어서 걸쭉하게 만들어요.
examples.en: You thicken sweet and sour sauce by adding starch water.
Rice contains a lot of starch.

examples.ko: 전분 가루가 없으면 밀가루로 대신해도 돼요?
examples.en: If I don't have starch powder, can I use flour instead?
Noodles made from potato starch are chewy.

examples.ko: 전분은 찬물에 잘 안 녹고 가라앉아요.
examples.en: Starch doesn't dissolve well in cold water and sinks.

explain: 요리에서는 '감자 전분', '옥수수 전분', '전분 가루'처럼 말하고, 같은 뜻으로 '녹말'도 써요. 영양이나 과학 이야기에서는 탄수화물의 한 종류로 나와요.

phrases.en: Dissolve the starch powder in water and add it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요리할 때 쓰는 하얀 가루를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the white powder used in cooking.

phrases.en: I made the batter with potato starch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무엇으로 만든 전분인지 말할 때 앞에 재료를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the ingredient in front to say what the starch is made from.

phrases.en: If you add starch, the soup gets thick.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전분과 같은 뜻이고 요리 이야기에서 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 전분 and used alongside it in cooking talk.

explain_en: In cooking it appears as '감자 전분', '옥수수 전분' and '전분 가루', and '녹말' is also used for the same thing. In nutrition and science talk it comes up as a kind of carbohydrate.

t90.ax: Rice contains a lot of starch.

examples.ko: 시장에서 정어리를 싸게 사서 구워 먹었어요.
examples.en: I bought sardines cheaply at the market and grilled them.

examples.ko: 정어리는 값이 싸고 영양도 많은 생선이에요.
examples.en: Sardines are a cheap and nutritious fish.
Tonight's side dish is braised sardines.
Fresh sardines came into the supermarket.

examples.ko: 정어리랑 고등어 중에 뭐가 더 좋아요?
examples.en: Which do you like better, sardines or mackerel?
I've never cooked with sardines.

explain: 생선 이름이라 '정어리 구이', '정어리 조림'처럼 요리 이름과 같이 자주 말해요. 모양이 비슷해 보이는 '멸치'와는 다른 생선이에요.

phrases.en: I ate grilled sardines for dinner.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생선을 구운 요리를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the dish of grilled fish.

phrases.en: My mother makes braised sardines very well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 양념에 졸인 반찬 이름으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common side dish name for sardines simmered in sauce.

phrases.en: I made a stew with canned sardines.
phrases.nuance_ko: 캔에 담긴 정어리를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to sardines sold in a can.

explain_en: It is a fish name, often used in dish names like '정어리 구이' (grilled sardines) or '정어리 조림' (braised sardines). It may look similar to '멸치' (anchovy), but it is a different fish.

en: to add; to supplement; to mix in

examples.en: I add a little salt when I cook.
No sugar was added to this snack.

examples.ko: 반죽에 우유를 첨가한 다음 잘 섞으세요.
examples.en: Add milk to the dough and then mix it well.
Fragrance was added to this shampoo.

examples.ko: 색소를 첨가하면 색이 더 진해질 거예요.
examples.en: If you add coloring, the color will get deeper.
This is bread made without preservatives.

explain: '넣다'는 어디에나 쓰지만 '첨가하다'는 음식, 약, 화학 제품에 무언가를 더할 때 주로 써요. 식품 성분표에는 '첨가물'이라는 말이 나와요. 글을 더할 때는 '덧붙이다'나 '추가하다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.example: 이 음식에는 첨가물이 들어 있지 않아요.
phrases.en: This food contains no additives.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식품에 더해 넣는 재료를 가리키는 명사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun for something added into food.

phrases.en: Vitamins have been added to this drink.
phrases.nuance_ko: '첨가하다'의 피동형으로, 이미 더해진 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form, describing something that has already been added.

phrases.en: I put a little more salt in the soup.
phrases.nuance_ko: '첨가하다'보다 일상에서 훨씬 자주 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A much more common everyday word than 첨가하다.

explain_en: Technical: add a substance to food or a mixture. 넣다 works almost anywhere, but 첨가하다 is used mainly for adding something to food, medicine or chemical products. On food labels you will see the word 첨가물 (additive). For adding words to a text, 덧붙이다 or 추가하다 sounds more natural.

t90.ax: I add a little salt when I cook.

examples.en: The security guards at our company work every other day.

examples.ko: 이 수업은 격일제라서 하루 걸러 가요.
examples.en: This class runs every other day, so I go every second day.

examples.ko: 격일제 근무는 하루 일하고 하루 쉬어요.
examples.en: With an every-other-day schedule, you work one day and rest the next.

examples.ko: 제가 격일제를 선택한 이유는 시간이 자유롭기 때문이에요.
examples.en: The reason I chose the every-other-day system is that my time is free.

examples.ko: 근무 방식이 격일제에서 매일 출근으로 바뀌었어요.
examples.en: The work system changed from every other day to daily attendance.
Many people say the every-other-day system is tough.

explain: '격일'은 하루를 거른다는 뜻이라, 격일제는 하루 걸러 하루 일하거나 운영하는 방식이에요. 근무나 수업, 운영 방식을 말할 때 써요. 한 해 걸러 하는 방식은 '격년제'예요.

phrases.en: From this month, I go to work every other day.
phrases.nuance_ko: '격일제로'보다 가볍게 주기를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Lighter than 격일제로; it just describes the cycle.

phrases.en: I run around the track every other day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '격일제' 대신 이렇게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In everyday talk, people say this instead of 격일제.

phrases.en: My father works on an every-other-day schedule.
phrases.nuance_ko: 근무 방식을 말할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for describing a work schedule.

explain_en: '격일' means skipping a day, so '격일제' is a system of working or operating every other day. It is used for work shifts, classes and operating schedules. Doing something every other year is '격년제'.

examples.en: The two roads cross in front of the market.
Sadness and joy mingled in my heart.

examples.ko: 두 선이 교차하는 곳에 점을 찍어요.
examples.en: I mark a dot where the two lines cross.

examples.ko: 서로 다른 의견이 교차할 때 토론이 재밌어요.
examples.en: A debate is fun when different opinions intersect.
It became awkward the moment people's eyes met.

examples.ko: 열차 두 대가 다리 위에서 교차할 거예요.
examples.en: Two trains will pass each other on the bridge.

explain: 교차하다는 선·길이 서로 가로질러 만나거나, 기쁨과 슬픔처럼 감정이 한꺼번에 오갈 때 써요. 두 길이 만나는 모습은 '만나다'로도 말해요. '감정이 교차하다'는 한국어에서 자주 나오는 표현이에요.

phrases.example: 두 길이 교차하는 곳에 편의점이 있어요.
phrases.en: There is a convenience store where the two roads cross.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장소를 설명할 때 자주 쓰는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common form for describing a location.

phrases.en: Expectation and anxiety mix together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 가지 마음이 한꺼번에 들 때 쓰는 자주 나오는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for two feelings arising at once.

phrases.en: The two roads do not cross.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서로 만나지 않는다는 뜻의 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, meaning they never meet.

explain_en: Active form; things cross or intersect each other, the more common choice (두 선이 교차하다). 교차하다 is used when lines or roads cut across each other, or when feelings such as joy and sorrow come and go together. Two roads meeting can also be said with '만나다'. '감정이 교차하다' is a very common Korean expression.

t90.ax: Sadness and joy mingled in my heart.

examples.en: Motorcycles are agile, so they are convenient for deliveries.
This team beat its opponent with its quick mobility.

examples.ko: 소방차의 기동력을 높이려면 길을 비켜 주세요.
examples.en: Please make way to help fire trucks move quickly.

examples.ko: 작은 회사의 기동력은 큰 회사보다 나아요.
examples.en: A small company's agility is better than a big company's.

examples.ko: 우리 팀에는 기동력 있는 선수가 필요해요.
examples.en: Our team needs a mobile, quick player.

examples.ko: 눈이 와서 구급차의 기동력에 문제가 생겼어요.
examples.en: Because of the snow, the ambulance had trouble getting around.

explain: '기동성'과 바꿔 쓰는 경우가 많아요. 차, 소방, 경찰, 스포츠, 회사 일처럼 상황에 맞게 빠르게 움직이는 이야기에 나와요.

phrases.en: This team is very mobile.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빠르게 움직일 수 있다고 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to praise the ability to move quickly.

phrases.en: I switched to a smaller car to increase mobility.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 빠르고 편하게 움직이게 만든다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means making movement faster and easier.

phrases.en: Mobility is important for deliveries.
phrases.nuance_ko: '기동력'과 바꿔 쓸 수 있는 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A near-synonym you can swap with 기동력.

explain_en: It is often interchangeable with '기동성'. It appears in talk about moving quickly as needed, such as cars, fire services, police, sports and company work.

t90.ax: Our team needs a mobile, quick player.

examples.en: These scissors are multipurpose, so they're really convenient.
I bought a multipurpose table and use it as a desk too.

examples.ko: 다용도 칼 하나면 캠핑 준비가 끝나요.
examples.en: One multipurpose knife is enough for camping.

examples.ko: 다용도로 쓸 수 있는 가방을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for a bag that can be used in many ways.

examples.ko: 이 세제는 다용도라서 주방과 욕실에 다 써요.
examples.en: This detergent is multipurpose, so I use it in the kitchen and bathroom.
A multipurpose chest of drawers makes it easy to organize.

explain: 한 물건을 여러 용도로 쓸 수 있을 때 써요. '다목적'과 비슷하지만 물건이나 도구에는 '다용도'를 더 자주 쓰고, 공간이나 시설에는 '다목적'을 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 이 상자는 다용도로 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You can use this box for many purposes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '로'를 붙여서 어떻게 쓰는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '로', it tells how something is used.

phrases.en: It's handy to have a multipurpose pair of scissors.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 도구 이름을 붙여서 여러 일에 쓰는 물건을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put before a tool name to mean an item with many uses.

phrases.en: We use this room for many purposes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻은 비슷하지만 공간이나 시설에 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar meaning, but more often used for spaces and facilities.

explain_en: Usable in many ways, esp. tools and products. It is used when one item serves several uses. It is close to '다목적', but '다용도' is more often used for items and tools, while '다목적' is common for spaces and facilities.

examples.en: We don't have unlimited time.

examples.ko: 이 일을 무한정 기다릴 수는 없어요.
examples.en: I can't wait for this forever.

examples.ko: 이 서비스는 무한정 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can use this service without limit.

examples.ko: 돈이 무한정 나오는 기계가 있으면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I wish there were a machine that gave out endless money.
I'm exhausted by the endlessly growing workload.

examples.ko: 음식을 무한정 시켜 먹을 수는 없어요.
examples.en: You can't order food endlessly.

explain: '무한정 기다리다', '무한정 쓰다'처럼 부사처럼 동사 앞에 붙여 쓸 때가 가장 많아요. '끝없이', '한없이'와 비슷하지만 '횟수나 양에 제한이 없다'는 느낌이 강하고, '~ㄹ 수는 없다' 같은 부정 표현과 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: You can't use water without limit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 양이나 횟수에 제한이 없다는 느낌으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Suggests no limit on amount or number of times.

phrases.en: Resources are not unlimited.
phrases.nuance_ko: '끝이 있다'는 뜻으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say that something has an end.

phrases.example: 이 도서관에서는 책을 제한 없이 빌릴 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You can borrow books from this library without limit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하고 더 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning but an easier phrase.

explain_en: It is mostly used like an adverb before a verb, as in '무한정 기다리다' or '무한정 쓰다'. It is similar to '끝없이' and '한없이', but stresses that there is no limit on amount or number, and it often appears with negatives like '~ㄹ 수는 없다'.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 직접 만든 수공품만 팔아요.
examples.en: This shop only sells handmade items.
Since they're handmade, no two look the same.
I bought a pretty handmade cup at the market.
Handmade goods are more expensive than machine-made ones.

examples.ko: 외국 친구에게 줄 수공품을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for a handmade gift for my foreign friend.

examples.ko: 이 마을 사람들이 직접 만든 수공품이에요.
examples.en: These are handicrafts made by the people of this village.

explain: '공예품'은 예술적인 솜씨가 들어간 물건을 말할 때 잘 어울리고, '수공품'은 기계가 아니라 손으로 만들었다는 점을 강조해요. 요즘은 '핸드메이드'라는 말도 많이 써요.

phrases.en: This bag is handmade.
phrases.nuance_ko: '수공품'과 뜻이 비슷하고, 요즘 가게에서 더 자주 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning to 수공품, and more common in shops today.

phrases.en: They sell handicrafts at the weekend market.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 사고파는 이야기에서 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about buying and selling.

phrases.en: I bought a cup at a handicraft shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수공품을 파는 가게를 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a shop that sells handmade goods.

explain_en: A finished article made by hand, sold in shops (장인) '공예품' (craft) fits objects with artistic skill, while '수공품' stresses that something was made by hand, not by machine. People also say '핸드메이드' (handmade) these days.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 와서 오늘 경기를 순연했어요.
examples.en: We postponed today's game because of the heavy rain.

examples.ko: 회사에서 행사 날짜를 다음 주로 순연하기로 했어요.
examples.en: The company decided to postpone the event to next week.
I heard they are postponing the show by a day because of the typhoon.

examples.ko: 일정을 순연하면 예약도 다시 해야 해요.
examples.en: If we postpone the schedule, we have to make the reservation again.
The weather is bad, so would it be okay to postpone the departure?
What was the reason for postponing the game?

explain: '연기하다'와 비슷하지만 경기나 행사 일정을 그대로 뒤로 미룰 때 뉴스에서 자주 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '미루다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: The game was postponed to tomorrow because of the rain.
phrases.nuance_ko: '순연하다'의 피동 표현으로, 일정이 저절로 뒤로 밀렸을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form of 순연하다, used when a schedule gets pushed back.

phrases.en: The coach postponed the training schedule.
phrases.nuance_ko: '일정'과 함께 쓰면 계획을 그대로 뒤로 미룬다는 뜻이 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 일정, it clearly means pushing a plan back as it is.

phrases.example: 비가 와서 약속을 다음 주로 미뤘어요.
phrases.en: It rained, so I put off the appointment until next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '순연하다' 대신 '미루다'를 더 자연스럽게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In everyday conversation, 미루다 sounds more natural than 순연하다.

explain_en: Formal; shift events like games to next scheduled slot, news. It is similar to '연기하다' (to postpone) but often appears in the news when a game or event schedule is pushed back as it is. In daily talk, '미루다' sounds more natural.

t90.ax: What was the reason for postponing the game?
